statement: The Owing is true at every line and still unjust.
Ussa-Rekh freed them and holds them still.
The well keeps failing because stone cannot hold in the moving clay bank: its lining has cracked and been mended every year, and the ford seeps in through the new crack.
Clay, the landing's own craft, would hold the well where stone cracks, so the landing could mend it without building in stone.
The landing's charge was set in answer to the station's rise, and the two together are driving travellers to wade at the crocodile's pool at night.
Something in the spring, not the food, is making people sick.
The courier did not leave; he was murdered and hidden in the spring.
Reeh-Shaal killed him.
The crew baited the shallows under the plank walk, and the bait drew the beast.
Sei-Wan is alive among the roots in the basin's shallows east of the gate, and a viper keeps him there.
The woman with the knotted cord came for the courier's satchel and for the cutting's sap, not for the gang, and chose to leave the player alive.
The cell came for the cutting's sap as much as for the satchel, with jars ready: a long work, not a raid.
The tree was cut, not sickened, and not by its tree-minder.
The cut sap went north to the cell's camp.
Kaska-Meen and Ei-Tuja have each half of it, and neither has seen a cut root.
The salt works are not the cause.
The salt comes up from a breach below the village.
The founders cut the breach to kill a rival grove.
The necklace can be had without harm, lifted off Keeps-What-Floats by day or while he sleeps, or talked off him.
All three clients lied about what the box holds for them.
Only one of the three can be freed, and the player decides which.
